column1: # OCTOPATH TRAVELER II: Square Enix / Acquire, Unreal Engine 4.27 (one pak with the shaders inline in the cooked packages, MallocBinned3), SDK 12.3.2, NVN, CRIWARE sound and movies;
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on the Mac (docs/agents)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game's Switch device profile caps Unreal at 30 (t.MaxFPS=30, and rhi.syncinterval=2, the present interval 2 it asks for while BaseSwitchEngine.ini's
# r.VSync=1 locks presents to vsync; its Windows, PS4 and PS5 profiles set t.MaxFPS=60); the host writes t.MaxFPS 60 and rhi.SyncInterval 1 into its console variables (hle_fpslock.c),
# so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power
# Unreal Engine 4.27: nninitStartup (main+0xbebd44) needs virtual address memory, sets a 6 MB heap for the C library's malloc and reserves one address region for the engine

# (62 GB by default; the rewriter's engine-wide gate on the store of its size (dm/tools/ue_region.py; hle_svc.c) gives it what the alias region has room for, 2.81 GB; until 2026-10-31 -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=2048 in game_args). Its allocator, an FMallocBinned3 made on the first allocation, cuts its pools out of that region; the

# constructor call is cut and the host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone outside the guest block (the rewriter's engine-wide cut, dm/tools/ue_malloc.py; hle_uemalloc.c layout UE4_27), and the SDK-wide rules cut the SDK's node
# area to 62 MB and align regions of 4 MB and more to 2 MB, as SDK 20 (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py, the SDK 12.3.2 build). Alias region = node area + the region (at alias +0.06 GB;
# until 2026-10-30 a 1 GB alignment put it at +0.75 GB) + 256 MB for regions made later; 256 MB stacks, 384 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
# The battle menu picks a weapon with the D-pad (its tutorial: "Select Attack and use + to choose a weapon"), which only the 3D pad layout has. It plays with the controller, so it stays
# docked (1920x1080). On the traveler selection, L / R step from traveler to traveler (moving the cursor onto one with the stick opened the card in one Mac run only)
# Unreal Engine 4.27 with no shader code archives: each material's shaders inline in its cooked package (.uexp) and the engine's global shaders in Engine/GlobalShaderCache-SF_GLSL_SWITCH.bin,
# every one an LZ4 block (shader_split.py ue_inline_shaders, uepak.py inline_shaders). Unreal combines vertex and pixel shaders per draw from its pipeline state, so every vertex shader is
# made to link with any pixel shader (shader_split.py separable_pairs)
